relations.note: Xšaθra embodies Ahura Mazdā’s effective, desirable dominion.
Ahura Mazdā creates or establishes Šahrewar within his ordered divine creation.
Šahrewar intercedes before Ohrmazd on behalf of deserving poor people.
Vohu Manah appears jointly with dominion and helps make good rule effective.
Vohu Manah precedes Šahrewar as his hierarchical superior in the divine order.

relations.myth: Dominion realized through truth and order
relations.note: Aša and dominion are jointly invoked as mutually supporting divine powers.
Šahrewar is described as Ardwahišt’s obedient servant.
Ārmaiti appears with dominion, and humans seek her aid in acquiring it.
Haurvatāt is named jointly with enduring dominion and the other divine powers.
Amərətāt is named jointly with enduring dominion and the other divine powers.

relations.myth: Collective invocation of the divine heptad
relations.note: Xšaθra Vairya belongs to and is invoked with the collective divine heptad.
A metallic fitting on Mithra’s chariot is called xšaθra vairya.
Mihr cooperates with Šahrewar’s metal and its protective weapons.

relations.myth: Guarding metallic weapons at Mount Alburz
relations.note: The Sun cooperates with Šahrewar’s metal and keeps metallic weapons at Mount Alburz.
Āsmān cooperates with Šahrewar’s material sphere, from which metal is derived.
Anagrān cooperates with Šahrewar’s metal within the ordered creation.

relations.myth: Melting metals for the final river
relations.note: Fire melts the mountain metals belonging to Šahrewar for the final purification.

relations.myth: Melting metals for the final river
relations.note: Airyaman joins Fire in melting Šahrewar’s metal during the renovation.

relations.myth: Defeat of oppressive rule at renovation
relations.note: Šahrewar seizes and defeats Sāwul, the demon embodying tyranny and bad rule.
Šahrewar participates in defeating Ahriman’s host, though no direct single combat occurs.

relations.myth: Molten metal poured into the demons’ breach
relations.note: Šahrewar pours molten metal into the breach through which the demons entered creation.

relations.myth: Greek interpretation of Oromazes’ six gods
relations.note: Plutarch’s Good Order or Lawfulness is probably a Greek rendering of Xšaθra Vairya.
